text:
A special counsel team on Wednesday raided the home of a former National Election Commission (NEC) chief over allegations he took improper overseas trips during his time in office.
Investigators from special counsel Lee Tae-han's team searched Roh Tae-ak's home and seized a cell phone and other evidence as part of their probe into various alleged irregularities at the election watchdog.
Roh has been accused of taking his wife on three overseas business trips using the NEC's money during his time in office from May 2022 until June this year, when he resigned over widespread ballot shortages in the June 3 local elections.
Lee's team said it launched the raid after detecting falsehoods in official reports written by an NEC official on the outcome of the trips.
Twelve personnel were mobilized in the search, including two prosecutors and seven investigators. The search warrant listed charges of embezzlement, the falsification of official documents and their use.
A prosecution-police task force had earlier secured evidence and testimony that an NEC employee had been assigned to assist Roh's wife during the overseas trips.
In trip reports, however, the employee described attending official events with Roh.
This was the first time a raid was conducted at his home. Roh was also formerly a Supreme Court justice.
A separate search was conducted at the NEC headquarters earlier Wednesday, the special counsel team said.
Since its launch last month, the special counsel team has been investigating the ballot shortages and other allegations of misconduct involving the NEC.
